briefFidelity: FAIL, and on three independent clauses I had already written down before I opened the brief. (1) The brief asks for ONE form; every token is a stack of six to fifteen translucent polygons whose overlaps are the main visual event, and the parts are provably separate because they move independently across states -- in 1283437 the bone disc vanishes under stress while the core diamond simultaneously grows. (2) The brief allows 'two values and a ground, no more'; I independently counted warm greys (a continuum, because alpha stacking generates intermediate values), a bone/parchment white, a saturated ochre accent and the near-black ground -- three-plus values plus ground, and 1835793 adds a second ground outright by sitting on a filled mid-grey panel. (3) The brief's one falsifiable mechanical claim is that the market changes SCALE rather than COMPLEXITY, contracting under drawdown. Under stress 1203347 and 1310661 GAIN a ring of orange beads that does not exist in neutral, 1283437 and 1243682 LOSE their backing disc entirely, and 1283437's core nearly doubles. That is elements added, elements deleted, and the core expanding under drawdown -- complexity change, composition rearrangement, and the wrong direction. Also 'held well clear of every edge' fails outright at 1985692 and 1446330, which run to and past the bottom of the tile. This is a competent collection, but it is not STELE.
composition: Within a frame the hierarchy is strong and correct: saturated ochre core beats grey shell beats bone disc beats black void, and it holds at every size. Between frames there is effectively zero compositional variation -- all twelve make the identical decision of a centred mass with a symmetric margin, so the brief's 'emptiness doing as much work as the mass' is present as quantity of black but not as a compositional choice that ever differs. The frame is not used, it is merely left empty around a floating object. 1985692 and 1446330 are the only two that engage an edge and both do it by spilling off the bottom, which reads as clipping rather than as a decision. 1835793 is the sole frame where the ground is filled, and it reads as a different render rather than a variant.
collectionCoherence: This is the strongest axis and it is genuinely well done. All twelve share the centred single mass, the shell-around-warm-core armature, the flat translucent polygon language and the same three-value palette, and I identified that common structure before reading any brief. 1203347, 1310661, 1366079, 1733538, 1561509 and 1985692 are unmistakably siblings. Even the loosest members, 1243682 and 1446330 with their bilateral lobes and 1991107 rotated onto its corner, still read as the same project. The single coherence break is 1835793, whose filled mid-grey background panel puts it outside the set on the one property every other token shares.
palette: The colour is clearly chosen and it is the most likeable thing here: warm neutral greys, a bone-parchment white and exactly one saturated ochre-amber, on near-black. Restricting saturation to a single hue makes the core read as the focus in every token without any other device, which is why 1203347 and 1733538 still work at 120px. But measured against the brief's explicit ceiling of two values and a ground it is over budget, and the translucent stacking makes it worse rather than better by generating a continuum of intermediate greys in 1446330 and 1475115. The ground supports the drawing everywhere except 1835793, where the mid-grey panel competes with and flattens the object sitting on it.
seedVariation: Sits in the safe middle but is thinner than twelve frames suggest, and it is thin in exactly the way the brief did not ask for. Variation is two independent picks from a small vocabulary -- outer silhouette (circle 1203347/1475115/1283437, hexagon 1310661/1366079/1733538, square 1561509/1985692/1835793, diamond 1991107, lobed 1243682/1446330) crossed with core shape (circle 1203347/1733538/1561509, diamond 1283437/1991107, square 1366079/1985692/1835793, blob 1475115). The brief wanted tokens to differ CHIEFLY in silhouette; here silhouette shares the work with core shape and with internal stack density, so the axis it named is diluted rather than absent. Nothing is so wide that the project stops being one project.
thumbnailSurvival: At 120px the twelve collapse to roughly six or seven distinguishable things. 1203347, 1733538 and 1561509 all reduce to grey-blob-with-orange-circle; 1366079 and 1985692 both reduce to grey-mass-with-orange-square. What survives is silhouette, the shell/core relation and the single accent -- which is enough to browse. What does not survive is internal structure: 1446330 and 1475115 become undifferentiated grey mush with no readable armature, and the stepped polygon edges that give 1985692 and 1561509 their character at 256 degrade into staircase noise. The 256 sheet confirms this is real detail being lost rather than detail that was never there, so the failure is one of scale robustness, not of emptiness.
marketResponse: Loudly visible and comprehensively not the change that was claimed. The stress row is instantly identifiable at 120px, but it is identifiable by TEMPERATURE -- the whole object swings to brown-amber in 1203347, 1310661 and 1243682 -- and the brief asked for scale with complexity held constant. What actually happens under drawdown is that content is added (a ring of orange beads appears along the top edge of 1203347 and 1310661 that is simply absent in neutral), content is deleted (1283437 and 1243682 lose their bone backing disc entirely), forms get spikier (1243682 and 1283437 gain angular projections), and the core EXPANDS -- 1283437's diamond nearly doubles under stress. Envelope and core therefore move in opposite directions, which is the precise opposite of 'one object breathing' and is instead a composition rearranging itself. Recovery does return to a cool, calmer, larger register (1203347 and 1283437 recovery are the palest and widest of their three), so the expansion half of the claim is partly honoured; the contraction half is delivered backwards for the element a viewer actually looks at.
tokenIdentity: Mostly holds, with one real casualty. 1203347 stays a disc with a core, 1243682 stays a lobed cluster and 1283437 keeps its shield-and-diamond armature across all three states, so a collector would recognise those tokens under drawdown. But 1310661 loses its defining hexagonal silhouette under stress and becomes a rounded brown mass -- the one property the brief says distinguishes tokens from each other is the property that dissolves in that state. 1283437 also swings circle to shield to circle as its backing disc leaves and returns, which is a silhouette change rather than a scale change. Identity survives on continuity of the core, not on continuity of the form.
artifacts: 1985692 is clipped at the bottom of the tile, the stepped grey mass running to and past the frame edge, and it carries heavy staircase aliasing on the same edge. 1446330's lower point reaches the very bottom edge. 1283437 neutral and stress both carry a small triangular tab hanging below and slightly detached from the main mass, which reads as a mistake rather than a foot. 1991107 has a stray grey circle hanging off the lower right of the diamond with no structural relationship to anything. 1310661's hexagon outline is broken on the right by the corner of an overlapping square poking through. 1561509's offset stack of squares reads as misregistration rather than as intent. The scattered tiny orange dots and squares in 1203347, 1366079, 1475115 and 1985692 are incidental decoration, which the brief specifically excludes.
reasoning: briefFidelity is a gate and this work fails it on the brief's own most specific and most falsifiable sentence. STELE asked for one austere centred form in two values and a ground, whose market response changes scale while holding complexity constant, contracting under drawdown. What is on the sheets is a composite object of many translucent stacked polygons in three-plus values plus an accent hue and, in 1835793, a second ground, whose stress state adds a bead ring to 1203347 and 1310661, deletes the backing disc from 1283437 and 1243682, and enlarges rather than contracts the core of 1283437 while the envelope shrinks around it. I wrote all of that down as a shell-and-core object with a temperature-driven state change before I had read a word of the brief, which is why I trust it. The work is not bad -- coherence is strong, the single-accent palette is genuinely well judged, and the state rows are unambiguous at browse size, which is more than most collections manage. It is refused because it is a different artwork from the one commissioned, executed well, and the gate does not care how well.
wouldChange: Make the state response actually scalar. Hold hue, value and element count fixed across neutral, stress and recovery, and drive a single uniform scale factor on the whole mass so 1283437 and 1203347 read as the same object at three sizes -- delete the stress bead rings on 1203347 and 1310661 and stop removing the backing disc from 1283437 and 1243682, since both are complexity edits standing in for a scale edit, and reverse the core's direction so it contracts rather than doubles under drawdown. Then collapse the palette to the brief's budget: one grey value, one bone value, the near-black ground, and either drop the ochre or promote it to be one of the two values rather than a fourth. Flatten each token to a genuinely single form so translucent overlap stops generating intermediate greys, which also fixes the 120px mush in 1446330 and 1475115. Give 1835793 the same black ground as the other eleven, pull 1985692 and 1446330 up off the bottom edge so the clearance rule holds, and delete the incidental marks -- the dots in 1203347 and 1475115, the stray circle on 1991107, the detached tab under 1283437. Push the remaining variation entirely into silhouette, which is where the brief put it and where this work is already closest to right.
